title: Declarative parameter profile registry with runtime validation adapters and progressive error messaging
creator: Maya Thompson
description: Problem: Customers integrating tool/function calling report two recurring issues: (1) divergent JSON schema shapes across SDKs and model variants cause brittle client-side validation; (2) opaque runtime validation errors are difficult to debug in production and lead to poor UX. Goal: introduce a declarative Parameter Profile Registry (PPR) that centralizes canonical parameter shapes (lightweight JSON SCHEMA+profile annotations), together with small runtime validation adapters that perform defensive coercion, version negotiation, and progressive error messages that guide remediation. This ticket scopes the server-side registry schema design, a minimal validation adapter interface, and a migration plan for instrumenting our runtime to emit actionable error envelopes (human-friendly + machine parsable) for tool calls.
acceptance_criteria: A canonical PPR JSON text format is documented and merged to docs/confluence with examples for primitive coercion, defaults, and deprecation hints
Runtime exposes an adapter interface (AdapterV1) that can be registered per-model/per-tool and invoked during the call validation phase
At least two adapters implemented: strict (reject on mismatch) and coercing (attempt safe coercions: numeric strings -> numbers, singleton -> list), exercised in unit tests

Validation failures produce an error envelope with: short_code, user_message, machine_hint, and optional remediation_actions (up to 3 suggestions). The envelope is emitted as structured telemetry and returned to SDKs where applicable
SDKs (JS + Python) receive consistent error envelope mapping in dev builds and surface user_message by default; integration tests confirm mapping
Migration plan with rollout gates and canary on 10% of hosted traffic documented with rollback criteria
technical_notes: Registry format priorities: readability, concise deprecation metadata, and minimal runtime footprint. Avoid full JSON Schema Draft complexity - prefer a constrained subset we can validate quickly
Suggested fields in PPR entries: name, version, type (string|number|boolean|array|object), nullable, default, coercion_rules (enum), deprecation (since, replacement), examples
Coercion rules should be explicit and opt-in per-profile to avoid surprising behavior. Examples: "coerce_numeric_strings", "tolerate_singleton_for_array"
Adapter interface (pseudo): validate(params, profile, context) -> {status: ok|error|coerced, params: normalized, errors: [envelope]}
Error envelope shape (string representation): short_code e.g. "PPR_TYPE_MISMATCH", user_message, machine_hint (structured string), remediation_actions (list of strings), telemetry_tags
Telemetry: emit validation latency, adapter_type, profile_version, short_code, and whether coercion occurred. Track user-facing error rate and mean time to fix for remediation guidance
Backcompat: support legacy-tool profiles by allowing profile.version negotiation and a compatibility mode flag in runtime that maps old schema keys to new names via a simple alias map
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (design): Finalize PPR subset and publish Confluence doc with examples and anti-patterns (owner: Maya) - 3 days
Phase 2 (runtime): Implement AdapterV1 interface and two adapters (strict, coercing). Hook into pre-routing validation pipeline; add unit tests (owner: Rohan) - 8 days
Phase 3 (SDK): Add error envelope mapping to JS/Python SDKs in dev release, add integration tests that simulate coerced and rejected calls - 5 days
Phase 4 (canary): Rollout PPR to 10% hosted traffic with validation telemetry and alerting, run for 1 week, iterate on messages and coercion rules based on early errors - 7 days
Phase 5 (rollout): Gradual increase to full rollout after acceptance gates met; publish migration guide and example upgrade patches for customers - 4 days
